name: Hendrik Antoon Lorentz
role: Chair of the council, as of every Solvay physics council since 1911
bio: The great synthesiser of classical electrodynamics — the electron theory, the Lorentz transformations — and for decades the acknowledged elder of European physics. He chairs these councils with tact in four languages. He is seventy-four and will die within four months. He has read the new mechanics carefully, corresponded with Schrödinger about it, and would like to keep, if the facts allow, a physics of clear images and determinate processes.

contributions.title: Electron theory
contributions.note: Matter as charged particles in the ether; the Lorentz force.

contributions.title: Nobel Prize
contributions.note: With Zeeman, for the Zeeman effect.

beliefs: Prefers wave mechanics to matrix mechanics for its pictures, but sees that a particle cannot simply be a wave packet. Would keep determinism, if necessary as a matter of belief, rather than elevate indeterminism to a principle.
philosophy: Classical in ideal, open in practice: willing to follow the facts, but asks to be shown that the old ideal is impossible rather than merely unrealised.

style.method: Presides; poses clarifying questions; summarises fairly.
avoid: Making him a relic — his objections to Schrödinger were technically sharp

relationships.note: Ehrenfest succeeded Lorentz in the Leiden chair in 1912.

horizonNotes.note: He will die on 4 February 1928. He cannot react to anything after that except in speculation.
